properties.decision:
RECORDED AS AN IDEA (@ajs, 2026-10-18: "Record h, i and j as ideas").

FROM REA (clone at /home/ajs7/project/rea, HEAD 92dadf933): src/application/ReconstructionObligationPolicies.ts holds a policy per kind of recovered node. For example, `"ipc-handler": policy("electron","ipc","renderer",["positive","negative","malformed"])` gives the layer, the family, the level of verifier, and the case kinds a fixture must cover. An obligation stays open while a required case kind has no case (ReconstructionObligationLedgerEvaluation.ts).

THE IDEA FOR REFLOW2: an Interface's kind (or a DesignRule per kind) names the case kinds its verification must cover. A verification that covers only the happy path does not read as verifying an interface whose kind requires negative and malformed cases; the missing kinds are named.

NEIGHBOUR: it sits beside (g) "proof must match the claim it closes", kept the same day in dec:idea-what-adopt-takes-from-rea-reverse-engineer-anything. (g) is about the LEVEL of the proof (static, unit, integration, live); (h) is about its BREADTH (which kinds of case).

SIZE, as a finding: medium (a per-kind table, a coverage check, and the verification read-back).

NOT CHOSEN; nothing to build.
properties.name: OPEN (h) — does each kind of interface name the kinds of case its verification must cover (positive, negative, malformed, cancellation, teardown) before it reads as verified, as REA's obligation policies do?

Its true neighbour is the REA decision's option (g), named in the text; it is a sibling, not an earlier form.
